newsitem.title: USA: Kurdish rival groups agree to resume peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish rival groups agree to resume peace talks.

text.p: Leaders of rival Kurdish factions have agreed to prepare to resume peace talks in the Turkish capital Ankara in the next few weeks, the State Department said on Friday.

In meetings on Thursday and on Friday in northern Iraq with two senior U.S. officials, the leaders of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) agreed to get ready for renewed peace negotiations, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said at a briefing.
"All sides agreed on the need for early and rapid preparation for a next high-level meeting in Ankara in the coming weeks," Burns said.

The two Kurdish groups battled for two months last year in northern Iraq, which has effectively been under Western protection since 1991, after the KDP sought aid from Iraqi forces to help it capture the city of Arbil from its rival.
The United States brokered a ceasefire in October, and the two groups have been conducting sporadic peace talks in Ankara since then.
The KDP walked out of the Ankara talks last month, accusing the PUK of killing one of its officials in the Iraqi Kurdish town of Halabja. The PUK denied the charge.
